subject: polity

subtopics.name: Constitutional Framework, Types & Composition of PSCs
subtopics.coverage: Articles 315 & 316: Establishment of UPSC, SPSC, JSPSC; Composition, Member Qualifications
tnpsc_traps: JSPSC is a statutory body created by Parliament, not constitutional
Strength of UPSC decided by President, SPSC by Governor

subtopics.name: Appointment, Tenure, Removal & Suspension
subtopics.coverage: Articles 316 & 317: Appointment authority, Tenure (6/65 vs 6/62), Resignation, Ground of Misbehavior, Supreme Court Inquiry, Suspension powers
key_concepts: Governor can only suspend SPSC member pending SC inquiry
Binding advice of SC on inquiry under Art 145
tnpsc_traps: Governor appoints SPSC members but ONLY President can remove them
Supreme Court inquiry report on misbehavior is binding on President

subtopics.name: Service Conditions & Post-Tenure Restrictions
subtopics.coverage: Articles 318 & 319: Protection of service conditions against disadvantage; Ineligibility for reappointment to same office; Prohibition of employment under GoI or State governments
key_concepts: Conditions cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment
UPSC Chairman completely barred from GoI/State employment
SPSC Chairman eligible for UPSC Chair/Member or other SPSC Chair
tnpsc_traps: UPSC members can become UPSC Chairman or SPSC Chairman, but cannot hold any other GoI/State office
SPSC member can become Chairman of that same SPSC

subtopics.name: Functions, Advisory Role & Legislative Extension
subtopics.coverage: Articles 320 & 321: Conduct of exams, recruitment, mandatory consultation in disciplinary cases, pension claims, reimbursement of legal expenses; Exclusion of SC/ST reservations and backward class claims under Art 320(4); Extension of functions by Parliament/State Legislature
key_concepts: Power to extend functions by Act of Legislature
Central Vigilance Commission relationship with UPSC
tnpsc_traps: UPSC consultation is NOT mandatory for reservation of appointments or posts for backward classes or SC/ST claims
UPSC is advisory; government can reject advice by submitting reasons to Parliament

subtopics.name: Expenses, Annual Reports & Independence Safeguards
subtopics.coverage: Articles 322 & 323: Expenses charged on Consolidated Fund (non-votable); Submission of annual reports to President/Governor; Memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice laid before Parliament/State Legislature; Institutional independence safeguards
key_concepts: Charged on Consolidated Fund of India/State
Annual report presented to President (UPSC) or Governor (SPSC)
Memorandum of non-acceptance must be approved by Cabinet and laid before legislature
tnpsc_traps: Non-acceptance of UPSC advice requires approval of Appointments Committee of Cabinet / Ministry of Personnel, not administrative ministry alone

important_cases: Hargovind Pant v. Dr. Raghukul Tilak (1979) - Governor office is not employment under GoI for Art 319
State of Uttar Pradesh v. Manbodhan Lal Srivastava (1958) - Article 320(3)(c) consultation is directory, not mandatory
Ram Ashray Yadav, Chairman Bihar PSC (2000) - Reference under Art 317(1) for removal
commissions_committees: Lee Commission (1924) - Recommended establishment of Public Service Commission in India
Government of India Act 1919 - First provision for Public Service Commission
Government of India Act 1935 - Federal Public Service Commission & Provincial PSCs
constitutional_provisions: Part XIV, Chapter II, Articles 315 to 323
Article 315: Public Service Commissions for Union and States
Article 316: Appointment and term of office of members
Article 317: Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission
Article 318: Power to make regulations as to conditions of service of members and staff
Article 319: Prohibition as to the holding of offices by members of Commission on ceasing to be such members
Article 320: Functions of Public Service Commissions
Article 321: Power to extend functions of Public Service Commissions
Article 322: Expenses of Public Service Commissions
Article 323: Reports of Public Service Commissions

tnpsc_traps.name: Removal of SPSC Member
tnpsc_traps.description: Governor appoints SPSC members, but ONLY the President can remove them.

tnpsc_traps.name: Joint State PSC Nature
tnpsc_traps.description: JSPSC is created by an Act of Parliament on request of State legislatures (statutory body), NOT directly established by Constitution.

tnpsc_traps.name: Tenure Differences
tnpsc_traps.description: UPSC members retire at 65; SPSC and JSPSC members retire at 62. Both have 6-year terms.

tnpsc_traps.name: Article 319 Bar
tnpsc_traps.description: UPSC Chairman cannot take ANY employment under GoI or State. SPSC Chairman can only be appointed as UPSC Chairman/member or other SPSC Chairman.

tnpsc_traps.name: Advisory Character
tnpsc_traps.description: UPSC advice is not legally binding on executive, but reasons for non-acceptance must be placed before Parliament.
